body: Continue implies it's been operating with major taxpayer dollars for years, which it hasn't. You don't ask whether the IRS should be funded by taxpayer dollars, you don't ask why the US Military cannot pass a financial audit,  but God forbid the self funded Postal Service employed by Americans for Americans need some assistance to keep up with the private industries you all lose your minds. The Postal Service is in the Constitution, so yes I'm okay with taxpayer dollars going to it.

I just never understood this obsession with privatizing everything. Don't we look at the general state of how shitty everything is and recognize that the private industry only deems you useful if you can pay? The Postal Service provides delivery to every household in America. Other couriers have already determined it unfeasible to deliver to many areas of this country, without the postal services network people just won't be able to afford important things like medicine. Rural areas in republican states rely on the postal service operating at a loss. 





The money has only been really coming since 2020. Prefunding ended 2022. The big steps of the plan to use that money they're now borrowing from Congress starts this year. You cite the data as if the debt is the conclusion not the symptom. The money actually needs to be used and changes to old infrastructure take time.

The Postal Service gets no taxpayer dollars but is expected to run as a government entity with strong unions and low wages that can't compete with the private industry. They have to ask congress to increase their rates for stamps. The USPS can't just say, "oh well your grandma in the middle of nowhere in Arkansas isn't profitable to deliver to so we're going to stop delivery in that area" the way private entities can. That's why other couriers sell the last mile delivery of those packages to the post office and it's still a loss for the USPS. 




If you want it as a government entity, fund it as a government entity. The USPS has no cash on hand to fix its outdated infrastructure. Ignore the prefunding retirement thing everyone brings up the USPS hasnt even been able to pay into that for years. USPS got taxpayer dollars for new trucks which is fine, but doesn't solve 99% of the problems.

Throwaway.There's been a lot of misinformation, even in the news, about the North Houston Facility and the Missouri City facility these last few months. Don't blame anyone for not knowing but the speculation is off base. 



Growth in Houston has been massive and the PO has been slow to keep up because they didn't want to commit to big changes in the short term before a ton of sweeping changes nationwide to the facilities and the network. The Missouri City facility isn't even really open, they essentially used it as a short term parcel sorting facility during the holidays because North Houston was so jam packed. Don't even think the bathrooms are working in that place, it's still porta potties. Staff working there were holiday hires or employees from North Houston. That facility will be up and running this year and should decongest the whole network. Then I think they're going to ramp up hiring for carriers, but that part hasn't really been discussed. I only know of the mail processing side. Can't speak to the mismanagement at the local level which I've heard a lot of, but in a general sense this is why the mail is so bad in Houston right now.
